Business Model & Growth Analysis
Based solely on the extracted evidence: NIKE operates in the consumer sector [P2] selling athletic footwear and apparel through what the company describes as a wholesale channel (referenced as a driver of the stated $52.8 billion revenue figure [S1]) alongside direct channels implied by the reference to marketplace execution [S4]. The company states growth is supported by wholesale growth and stabilization across core categories [S1], and that it is investing in sport, product innovation, and brand demand creation [S4] as growth levers. Digital growth is referenced in the company's own framing [S6], though no quantified digital revenue or penetration figure appears in the evidence. How revenue is split across geographies, channels, or product categories is not found in the extracted evidence. The company identifies Greater China as an important market [S3] but provides no revenue attribution to that segment in the available material. Customer type (consumer end-user vs. wholesale retail partner) and pricing architecture are not described in the extracted evidence.
Information Readiness
Score: 22/100
Present:
• Company-stated revenue figure (period unconfirmed) [S1, C2]
• SEC EDGAR FY2026 revenue establishing an independent baseline of $46.4 billion [C2]
• Company-stated headcount of 81,500 [S2]
• High-level strategic direction (rebalancing, innovation investment) [S4]
• Geographic risk flag (Greater China) [S3]
• Competitive environment acknowledgment [S5]
• Public company stage confirmed [P1]
Needs Validation:
• Revenue period clarification — company-stated $52.8 billion vs. SEC-established $46.4 billion cannot be compared without knowing the company figure's fiscal year
• Gross margin and operating margin
• Segment revenue breakdown (geography, channel, product)
• Digital revenue and growth metrics
• Cash flow and balance sheet data
• Named leadership and management credentials
• Quantified impact of marketplace rebalancing initiative
• Headcount reconciled to an external source
Next evidence to supply: Audited income statement and segment disclosures for the same fiscal period as the company-stated $52.8 billion revenue figure, to resolve the 13.8% discrepancy with SEC EDGAR data and enable margin and segment analysis.

What Would Change the Picture
